title: Normal unipotent images under quotient homomorphisms
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a$ and $\mathbf G_m$ for [def-sc-gm-ga]. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars along the coordinate-algebra map is exact and detects zero modules. Let $f:A\to D$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism, and let $N\subseteq A$ be a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Here unipotent means that every geometric point is a unipotent matrix in a faithful linear representation [def-sc-general-linear-group], that is, $(n-I)^m=0$ for some $m\geq1$. Suppose $f|_N=j\circ u$ with $u:N\to I$ a faithfully flat homomorphism, $I$ an affine group scheme of finite type, and $j:I\hookrightarrow D$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $I$ is smooth, connected and unipotent, and $j(I)$ is normal in $D$. Neither kernel is required to be smooth, finite or central.

source.place: Corollary 14.7, printed p.282 (quotients of unipotent groups); Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.25 (smooth quotients), and Proposition 5.59(b), printed p.114 (connected quotients); proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400 (normality of the image under a surjective homomorphism).

proof.text: Put $C=F[I]$, $B=F[N]$, $E=F[D]$, and $P=F[A]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective], $u^*:C\to B$ and $f^*:E\to P$ are injective. Every injective $F$-linear map has an $F$-linear left inverse: extend a basis of its image and project. Tensoring these left inverses proves injectivity of $u^*\otimes u^*$, $f^*\otimes u^*$, and $u^*\otimes_F1_L$ for any field extension $L/F$. Products and scalar extensions have the tensor coordinate rings of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [def-weil-closed-immersion], an affine map factors through a closed subscheme exactly when its coordinate map kills the defining ideal, by the universal property of a quotient ring. Thus injective coordinate pullback detects equality of affine morphisms and factorization through closed subschemes. In particular $j$ is a homomorphism: its multiplication compatibility holds after $u\times u$, since $f|_N=j u$ and $u$ are homomorphisms, and $u^*\otimes u^*$ is injective; its identity and inverse compatibilities follow from the same equation and injectivity of $u^*$.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24, injective coordinate pullback; affine details expanded here. Stacks Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: Smoothness of $N\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ gives geometrically reduced fibres by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]; since the base is a field this says that $N_L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/F$. Its coordinate ring $B\otimes_F L$ has no nonzero nilpotents by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The injection $C\otimes_F L\hookrightarrow B\otimes_F L$ from step 1 implies that $C\otimes_F L$ also has no nonzero nilpotents: a nilpotent maps to zero, and injectivity then makes it zero. Thus $I$ is geometrically reduced. The finite-type group scheme $I$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth]. This does not assert that $u$ or its kernel is smooth.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24, via geometrically reduced coordinate rings and Proposition 1.28; Stacks 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal), 047N and 047P.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], $u:N\to I$ is surjective on underlying spaces. If $I$ were partitioned into two nonempty clopen subsets, their inverse images would partition $N$ into two nonempty clopen subsets, contradicting [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The scheme $I$ is nonempty because it has its identity point. Hence $I$ is connected.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(b), printed p.114, by the elementary topological argument; Stacks Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: For every algebraically closed extension $K/F$, we first prove that $N(K)\to I(K)$ is surjective. In affine coordinates $C_K=K\otimes_F C$ and $B_K=K\otimes_F B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The map $C_K\to B_K$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]: its target identifies with $C_K\otimes_C B$ by the maps on pure tensors. The algebra $B$ is finitely generated over $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], so the same finite generators generate $B_K$ over $K$. A point $x\in I(K)$ is a surjective $K$-algebra map $C_K\to K$; let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal kernel. The fibre algebra $T=B_K/\mathfrak m B_K$ is nonzero by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideal-nonzero], and is finitely generated over $K$, by the images of those generators. Choose a maximal ideal of $T$ by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal]. Its closed point has residue field $K$ over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. The resulting $K$-algebra map $B_K\to T\to K$ restricts to $x$ on $C_K$, since that restriction factors through $C_K/\mathfrak m=K$. It therefore gives a lift of $x$.

source.place: Corollary 14.7, printed p.282, quotient input, expanded on geometric points; Stacks Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), and faithfully flat fibres. This is an agent-written affine point-lifting argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-central-torus-faithful-weight-blocks] to $H=I$ and the trivial central subgroup $T=\{1\}\simeq\mathbf G_m^0$. It is closed because its coordinate map is the surjective counit $C\to F$. This gives a closed-immersion representation $\rho:I\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with $V$ finite-dimensional and nonzero; choose a basis to write its target as $\operatorname{GL}_{d,F}$, $d\geq1$. The closed-immersion coordinate quotient makes $\rho(R)$ injective for every $F$-algebra $R$ by the quotient universal property. Let $i:N\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,F}$ be the faithful representation in the hypothesis. Fix any algebraically closed extension $K/F$ and any $x\in I(K)$. Step 4 supplies $n\in N(K)$ with $u(n)=x$. The representation $i_K$ is faithful on every $K$-algebra, since each is also an $F$-algebra, and $i_K(n)$ is unipotent by the hypothesis on all geometric points of $N$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-representation-unipotent-point] over $K$ to $G=N_K$, faithful $i_K$, the representation $r=(\rho u)_K$, and the point $n$. It yields $(\rho(x)-I_d)^M=0$ for some $M\geq1$. This holds for every geometric point $x$ in the same faithful representation $\rho$, precisely the unipotence required in the statement.

source.place: Corollary 14.7, printed p.282, via preservation of unipotent elements under homomorphisms (§§9.19--9.21, printed p.171); Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, printed p.87, for the faithful representation (trivial-torus specialization of the cited existing node).

proof.text: Let $J=\ker(j^*:E\to C)$, the defining ideal of $j(I)\subseteq D$, and let $c:D\times I\to D$ be $(d,x)\mapsto d j(x)d^{-1}$. The composite $c\circ(f\times u):A\times N\to D$ sends $(a,n)$ to $f(a n a^{-1})$. Normality of $N$ in $A$, in the sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], says that $a n a^{-1}$ belongs to $N(R)$ for every $F$-algebra $R$. Evaluate at the universal pair over $P\otimes_F B$; the affine quotient criterion of step 1 then shows that the conjugation morphism $A\times N\to A$ factors through $N$. Consequently $c\circ(f\times u)$ factors through $I$ using $f|_N=j u$, so $(f^*\otimes u^*)c^*(J)=0$. The tensor injection of step 1 gives $c^*(J)=0$. Thus $c$ factors through $I$ as a morphism of schemes, including on nonreduced test algebras. For every $R$ and $d\in D(R)$ this yields $d j(I(R))d^{-1}\subseteq j(I(R))$; applying the same inclusion to $d^{-1}$ gives equality. Hence $j(I)$ is normal in $D$. Together with steps 2, 3 and 5 this proves every clause, with neither kernel assumed smooth, finite or central.

Milne 14.7 and 1.62 are about quotient homomorphisms, both citers (central-isogeny step 1 via affine-homomorphism-flat-image, quotient-borel-torus-images step 5) supply u as a homomorphism, and step 5 needs it so that ρu is a homomorphism. It is not a weakening. Step 1: faithfully-flat-universally-injective with N=R makes u* and f* injective, so the tensor maps are injective; the closed-subscheme factorisation test is right; j is a homomorphism (checked after precomposing with u×u; the identity is preserved since e_I=u e_N). Step 3: surjectivity on spectra plus a clopen partition and nonemptiness gives connectedness (5.59(b)). Step 4: for every algebraically closed K, base change of faithful flatness, nonzero fibre T, a maximal ideal, and closed-point-residue-field-base give a K-point lifting x; it uses no surjectivity on R-points.
